chapter-1/index.title: Chapter 1: Why Physical AI Matters
chapter-1/index.description: This chapter provides an overview of Physical AI, establishing the foundational concepts that will be built upon throughout the book.

chapter-1/topic-1.title: Why Physical AI Matters
chapter-1/topic-1.description: Humanoid robots are poised to excel in our human-centered world because they share our physical form and can be trained with abundant data from interacting in human environments. This represents a significant transition from AI models confined to digital environments to embodied intelligence that operates in physical space.

chapter-1/topic-2.title: Hardware Requirements
chapter-1/topic-2.description: This course is technically demanding. It sits at the intersection of three heavy computational loads: Physics Simulation (Isaac Sim/Gazebo), Visual Perception (SLAM/Computer Vision), and Generative AI (LLMs/VLA).

chapter-2/index.title: Chapter 2: The "Physical AI" Edge Kit & Robot Lab
chapter-2/index.description: This chapter explores the components required for your Physical AI development environment, from edge computing to robot hardware options.

chapter-2/topic-1.title: 2. The "Physical AI" Edge Kit
chapter-2/topic-1.description: Since a full humanoid robot is expensive, students learn "Physical AI" by setting up the nervous system on a desk before deploying it to a robot. This kit covers Module 3 (Isaac ROS) and Module 4 (VLA).

weeks-3-5/building-packages.title: Building ROS 2 Packages with Python
weeks-3-5/building-packages.description: ROS 2 packages are the fundamental building blocks of ROS applications. A package contains the source code, launch files, configuration files, and all other resources needed for a particular functionality. Creating well-structured packages is essential for developing maintainable and reusable robot software.

weeks-3-5/intro.title: Weeks 3-5: ROS 2 Fundamentals
weeks-3-5/intro.description: This section covers the core fundamentals of ROS 2 (Robot Operating System 2), the middleware framework that connects all the components of your robotics system together.

weeks-3-5/ros2-architecture.title: ROS 2 Architecture and Core Concepts
weeks-3-5/ros2-architecture.description: ROS 2 (Robot Operating System 2) is a flexible framework for developing robotic applications. Unlike traditional software frameworks, ROS 2 is designed for distributed systems, real-time operation, and resource-constrained environments.

weeks-3-5/ros2-core-concepts.title: ROS 2 Core Concepts and Design Patterns

weeks-6-7/gazebo-environment.title: Gazebo Simulation Environment
weeks-6-7/gazebo-environment.description: Gazebo is a 3D simulation environment that provides realistic physics simulation, high-quality graphics, and convenient programmatic interfaces for developing and testing robotic applications. It's widely used in the robotics community for algorithm development, robot testing, and validation before deployment to real hardware.

weeks-6-7/intro.title: Weeks 6-7: Robot Simulation with Gazebo
weeks-6-7/intro.description: This section covers the fundamentals of robot simulation using Gazebo and other simulation tools, which are crucial for developing and testing robotics applications before deployment to real hardware.

weeks-6-7/physics-simulation.title: Physics Simulation in Robotics
weeks-6-7/physics-simulation.description: Physics simulation is the core of realistic robot simulation, enabling accurate interaction between robots and their environment. Proper physics simulation allows for realistic testing of robot behaviors, validation of control algorithms, and prediction of real-world robot performance before deployment on physical hardware.

weeks-6-7/robot-description.title: Robot Description: URDF and SDF Formats
weeks-6-7/robot-description.description: Robot description is fundamental to robotics simulation and development, providing accurate representations of robot geometry, kinematics, and dynamics. Proper robot descriptions are essential for successful simulation and control, enabling accurate physics simulation, collision detection, and visualization.

weeks-6-7/unity-simulation.title: Unity for Robot Simulation and Visualization
weeks-6-7/unity-simulation.description: Unity has emerged as a powerful platform for robotics simulation and visualization, offering high-quality graphics rendering, real-time physics simulation, and extensive development tools. Originally a game development platform, Unity has been adapted for robotics applications through specialized packages and plugins that enable robot simulation, perception system testing, and human-robot interaction development.

weeks-6-7/urdf-sdf.title: URDF and SDF Robot Description Formats
